claims.text: Headline: US blockades Iranian ports, oil surges
claims.note: CNN (Hanna Ziady) via CNN Newsource, 13 April: US Central Command said on 12 April it would block all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports from 10am ET on Monday 13 April; Brent rose 7% to $102 and WTI 7.8% to $104. Not ships bound for non-Iranian ports. Headline reworded (comma list).

edits.headline: Oil prices jump on US plan to blockade Iranian ports
edits.subheadline: Brent crude rose 7% to $102 a barrel after the US said it would block shipping to and from Iranian ports, CNN reported.
editorialBody: US Central Command said on 12 April that naval forces would block all maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports from 10am ET on 13 April, CNN reported. Ships travelling through the Strait of Hormuz to and from other countries' ports would not be stopped, it said.
Brent crude rose 7% to $102 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate rose 7.8% to $104, CNN reported.
The announcement came after talks between the US and Iran in Pakistan ended without agreement, the Associated Press reported.

Peter Magyar was projected to end Viktor Orban's 16 years as Hungary's prime minister after the 12 April election, CNN reported. Magyar, a former government insider, had promised to dismantle Orban's political system "brick by brick", AFP reported.
